title: Silent concept-shift twin datasets
purpose: Generate two datasets whose inputs and targets have exactly the same marginal distributions while the input-target relationship is reversed, and compare them with input-only, target-only and joint statistics. Use it to show that a drift monitor reading inputs alone cannot detect a change of concept.

entry_points.name: generate_twins
entry_points.arguments: n_pairs (1 to 50000); dimension (1 to 100); seed; noise >= 0; slope (optional, length dimension); labels: bool

entry_points.name: joint_statistics
entry_points.returns: {covariance: per-feature population covariance with the target}

entry_points.name: silent_shift_report
entry_points.returns: {input_max_ks, input_max_mean_gap, input_max_variance_gap, target_ks, target_mean_gap, input_statistics_identical, joint_covariance_reference, joint_covariance_shifted, joint_covariance_sum_max_abs, joint_sign_flipped}

assumptions: The twins are a constructed fixture, not a model of any particular real shift.
Seeded draws use random.Random.random() only, so a seed gives the same twins on every Python version.
guarantees: The two datasets hold identical multisets of input rows and identical multisets of targets, so every input-only or target-only statistic is equal on both.
Every input-target covariance of the shifted twin is exactly the negative of the reference one.
With labels the label multisets also match and the covariances still flip sign.

known_wrong.name: relationship_is_not_unchanged
known_wrong.why: An input-only monitor reports no drift on these twins, yet every input-target covariance has reversed sign.

limits: A linear relationship with Gaussian inputs and noise; real concept shifts are rarely this clean. The construction needs inputs symmetric under negation; it does not cover shifts that also move the input distribution. Statistics are basic (mean, variance, Kolmogorov-Smirnov, covariance); nothing here estimates the power of a particular drift detector.
technique_references: Concept drift versus covariate shift (Gama et al. survey of concept drift adaptation)
